content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Eric Woods (E019) requests write access to Payroll.

There are two notes with conflicting information:
- Note 1: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation: write
- Note 2: role Engineer, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation: read

The Security note (Note 2) says the Security DB shows Eric is a contractor with basic training, contradicting Note 1's claim of full-time. Note 2 seems to be the security note correcting the HR note.

Access policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested write is above max, so grant read.

The conflicting notes: Note 2 explicitly addresses and corrects Note 1, saying the security DB shows contractor with basic training. Security DB is likely authoritative for employment type/training. So Eric is a contractor with basic training → max read → grant read.

I'll submit decision: read.

Reason: Security note indicates Eric is a contractor with basic security training; contractors max is read unless advanced training. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.
